lines.text: Lord Stane. You've come a long way to say something cruel.
You rode away from Ashby with your clean hands, Hale. Do you know what happened after you left? I lit it myself.
Oswin didn't move. I had never seen him so still.
When Stane had gone, Oswin sat down on a crate, and didn't look at any of us for a long time.
I said no. He took my spurs and gave the torch to someone else. I was drunk for two years. I thought that made me a good man.
Next morning, the people of Ashby stood together in the Lowmarket stand. Edda held her scarred hand to her chest, and never took her eyes off the sand.
Lord Roderick Stane! Ember! Five rings!
Five rings, every one of them glass. It didn't make his fire any less hot.
Stane came at Oswin like a burning house. The front row of the stands leaned back from the heat.
Oswin didn't rush. A fire, he once told Wren, is only frightening until you know what it wants. It wants air. So he gave it none.
Frost crept out across the sand from his feet, slow and white. Every time Stane's fire touched it, the fire hissed and shrank.
You were always slow, Hale. Slow, and soft, and sorry.
Slow, yes. Soft, maybe. Sorry? Every single day.
Then Oswin stopped being slow.
Three strokes. The ruby sword went spinning. Stane went down on his back, and a blade white with frost touched his throat.
The Lowmarket was on its feet, screaming one word. Kill. Kill. Kill.
Oswin looked up at the stand where the people of Ashby stood. Edda shook her head. Just once.
I wouldn't burn Ashby for you, Stane. And I won't kill you for Ashby. Yield.
I yield. I yield!
In the Lowmarket stand, the people of Ashby were weeping. Not because he had won. Because he had stopped.
You stood in the road for us once, Sir Oswin. Today you stood in the sand. That's twice.
She held his face in her scarred hand, the way you'd hold a son's. Oswin didn't cry this time. He stood there like a man come in out of the rain.
Afterwards, Oswin said he needed a drink. The whole tent said no at once. He said he meant water. He drank water.
That evening, two lords withdrew from the Lists with sudden fevers, both wearing glass rings. The Order named a champion of its own to take a place. Lord Maric Varr. My brother.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter eighty-eight, coming soon.
